indicators.note: something stored in a container sits inside it, so the paper goes into the folder

parts.note: a file is a folder for papers
a rag is slang for a cheap newspaper

explanation.surface: A thin sheet of paper has been tucked away in a folder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' looks like part of the definition, but here it means a newspaper in its disparaging slang sense; 'stored in' puts it inside the folder word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flimsy is easily broken or damaged, which is the sense of delicate or breakable.

definitions.meaning: the title of Sitwell's sequence of poems set to music by William Walton
a false outward show put on for others

explanation.definitionFit: Sitwell's 1922 entertainment with Walton bears this title; and a pretence or false front is a superficial show.

clue.text: Outré images offensive to the elderly

indicators.note: outré means bizarre or unconventional, so the letters are put into an unusual order

explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' is a noun here: a campaign against older people, which is what the discrimination amounts to.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrimination or prejudice against people because of their age, especially the old, is an attack on older people.

definitions.meaning: taking part in a sporting contest
when it actually came to it

explanation.definitionFit: An athlete entered for a contest is taking part; the phrase also means 'as things turned out'.

indicators.note: to utter is to say aloud, so the word for a bore is pronounced

parts.note: an eagre is a tidal bore, a wave surging up a river

explanation.surface: Someone is a complete bore, yet enthusiastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning complete, but it is a verb: the tidal-wave word EAGRE is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being keen means being enthusiastic and impatient to do something.

clue.text: Keep returning Manx cat to haven

indicators.note: returning means the shortened cat word comes back the other way, read from right to left
a Manx cat is famously tailless, so the cat word loses its final letter

parts.note: puss is an everyday word for a cat
a port is a safe harbour or haven for ships

explanation.surface: A tailless cat from the Isle of Man keeps coming back to a safe place.
explanation.walkthrough: Manx cats are born without a tail, so 'Manx' cuts the last letter from the cat word, and 'returning' then reads what is left (PUS) backwards as SUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep someone is to maintain or provide for them financially, a sense of sustain.

indicators.note: imposes means one piece is laid on top of the next in this down clue

parts.note: states are conditions, as in a state of affairs
Man is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A member of parliament sets terms on an island community.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'imposes' means the conditions word is laid on top of the island; the Isle of Man is a self-governing island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An MP can be a respected political leader, and a statesman is a skilled, experienced politician.

clue.text: Penny constantly looks for an equal

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for penny or pence
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning constantly

explanation.surface: Penny is always searching for someone who matches her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks' tempts as the definition (to peer is to look), but the definition is 'an equal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is someone of the same standing or age, as in being judged by a jury of your equals.

definitions.meaning: inventive and new in thinking
existing at the very beginning

explanation.definitionFit: Inventive work is fresh and imaginative; the first version of something existed at its beginning.

definitions.meaning: a factory or industrial site
everything required, as when ordering a burger with every topping

explanation.definitionFit: A plant is a factory, also called works; and asking for everything on offer is a colloquial idiom.

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative in British politics
the left is the socialist wing of politics

explanation.surface: A split between Tories and socialists in a coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleft is a split or fissure, as in a cleft chin or a cleft in a rock.

definitions.meaning: the plants on which wine fruit grows
an informal route by which rumour passes from person to person

explanation.definitionFit: Vines bearing grapes make wine; and hearing something on the rumour mill means learning it through informal gossip channels.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Core adherent is devastated (10)': the anagram of 'adherent is' gives DISHEARTEN, but 'Core' cannot define it; the setter's word was probably 'Cow' and no source confirms it

clue.text: From tel Aviv I got to Spanish port

indicators.note: From says the answer is taken out of the run of letters that follows it

explanation.surface: Someone travelled from Tel Aviv to a port in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of letters in 'Aviv I got' supplies the port, straddling three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigo is a major fishing port on the Atlantic coast of Galicia in north-west Spain.

clue.text: Sadly, credit isn't given in bars

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Unfortunately pubs do not let you run a tab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like pubs, but it is a verb meaning prohibits.
explanation.definitionFit: To interdict something is to prohibit it formally, so it bans or bars.

parts.note: sailors are called jacks or jack tars, so every sailor in the fleet suggests an idiom for absolutely everybody

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means every single person without exception, and a sailor is traditionally called a jack.

indicators.note: found on places the first piece above the second in a down entry

parts.note: something rare is seldom seen
earth means land or ground

explanation.surface: A chemical element that is hardly ever found on dry land.
explanation.definitionFit: The lanthanide metals such as cerium are a group of chemical elements known by this name.

clue.text: A call for help about worst insulating material

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other, so the distress call surrounds the verb

parts.note: SOS is the Morse distress signal
to worst someone is to defeat them, the same as to best them

explanation.surface: A distress call goes out about the poorest insulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worst' looks like an adjective but is a verb meaning defeat; 'about' puts the defeat word inside the distress call.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous mineral was widely used to insulate buildings against heat and fire.

clue.text: His progeny must be tolerant, they say

indicators.note: they say tells us the word for being tolerant is pronounced, not written

parts.note: to forbear is to be patient and refrain from reacting

explanation.surface: A father's children have to put up with things, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: an ancestor is the one whose progeny they are, so 'His progeny' points back to him.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is someone from whom later descendants come, so the progeny belong to him.

clue.text: Noel arranges make-up for classy London girl

indicators.note: the make-up of something is how it is composed, so these letters are composed afresh

explanation.surface: Noel is applying cosmetics for a posh young Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' reads as cosmetics but signals that the twelve letters of NOEL ARRANGES are rearranged; 'arranges' is fodder, not the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sloane Ranger is a stereotypical wealthy, upper-class young person from the Chelsea area of London, named after Sloane Square.

definitions.meaning: a small part taken to show what the whole is like
to try something out

explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a representative piece; and to try food or a product is to taste or test it.

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'models' suggests catwalk work, but here it means perfect examples to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A model is a perfect example or standard to aim for, an ideal.

indicators.note: taking the top off a word drops its first letter

parts.note: to sever something is to cut it

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep trimming the top off something.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means at all times, as in 'ever hopeful'.

definitions.meaning: the pointer on a clock face that counts the smallest unit of time
previously owned by somebody else

explanation.definitionFit: A watch has hour, minute and seconds pointers; goods already owned by someone are described as used or pre-owned.

definitions.meaning: an assault or onslaught
the beginning of something

explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught by an enemy is an assault; the beginning of an illness or winter is its commencement.

clue.text: Some aspiring actors long for it

definitions.meaning: a portion of something
a role in a play, which would-be performers crave

explanation.definitionFit: A portion is a piece of the whole; and an actor wants to be cast in a role.

clue.text: It should define the s. African aurochs

parts.note: taken as written
SA is the abbreviation for South Africa or South African
the urus is another name for the aurochs, the extinct wild ox

explanation.surface: A reference book ought to explain what a South African wild ox is.
explanation.walkthrough: The urus or aurochs is an extinct European wild ox, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference book of synonyms explains words by offering equivalents, so it is expected to define them.

clue.text: Business couple meet one oil producer

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
PR is an abbreviation for pair, a couple
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A married pair running a company meet a supplier of oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra is dried coconut kernel, from which coconut oil is pressed.

clue.text: What a prisoner hates to exaggerate

definitions.meaning: a slang term for a period of time served in jail
to extend the truth beyond its real limits

explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner doing time serves a term in jail; stretching the truth means overstating it.

clue.text: Son tucked into common potatoes for samples

indicators.note: one thing tucked into another sits inside it, so the son goes inside the potatoes

parts.note: taters is a colloquial or vulgar word for potatoes; common marks it as slang
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A boy is eating ordinary spuds to try some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating, but it puts S inside TATERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasters are small portions offered so you can try something, the same as samples.
